functions.name: addBunApp
functions.description: Adds a Bun application to the application model. Bun should be available on the PATH.
functions.remarks:
This method executes the script directly using `bun <script>`. Bun natively runs JavaScript and TypeScript
files so no transpile step is required.
If the application directory contains a `package.json` file, Bun will be added as the default package manager.
When publishing to a container, the default base image is `oven/bun:1` for both the build and runtime stages.
functions.signature: addBunApp(name: string, appDirectory: string, scriptPath: string): BunAppResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the resource.

parameters.name: appDirectory
parameters.description: The path to the directory containing the Bun application.

parameters.name: scriptPath
parameters.description: The path to the script (for example, `server.ts`) relative to `appDirectory` to run.

functions.name: addDenoApp
functions.description: Adds a Deno application to the application model. Deno should be available on the PATH.
functions.remarks:
In run mode this method executes the script directly using `deno run -A <script>`. Generated
containers use the more restrictive `deno run --allow-net --allow-env <script>` default. Deno
natively runs JavaScript and TypeScript files so no transpile step is required. Deno's built-in OpenTelemetry
integration is enabled via the `OTEL_DENO` environment variable, so traces, metrics, and logs flow to the
Aspire dashboard with no application-level SDK wiring.
The full Deno flag surface (granular permissions, `--config`/`--import-map`/`--lock`, unstable
features, `--watch`, inspector flags, script args, and the `run`/`task`/`serve` sub-command
modes) can be configured with the fluent `WithDeno*` methods (for example `WithDenoAllow`,
`WithDenoConfig`, `WithDenoUnstable`, `WithDenoServe`). Configuring any of
these fully replaces the default arg vector, so a Deno workload never has to fall back to `AddExecutable`.
If the application directory contains a `package.json`, `deno.json`, or `deno.jsonc` file, Deno will
be added as the default package manager. When publishing to a container, the default base image is
`denoland/deno:2.9.0` for both the build and runtime stages.
functions.signature: addDenoApp(name: string, appDirectory: string, scriptPath: string): DenoAppResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the resource.

parameters.name: appDirectory
parameters.description: The path to the directory containing the Deno application.

parameters.name: scriptPath
parameters.description: The path to the script (for example, `main.ts`) relative to `appDirectory` to run.

functions.name: addJavaScriptApp
functions.description: Adds a JavaScript application resource to the distributed application using the specified app directory and run script.
functions.remarks:
If a Dockerfile does not exist in the application's directory, one will be generated
automatically when publishing. The method configures the resource with Node.js defaults and sets up npm
integration.

parameters.name: runScriptName

functions.name: addNextJsApp
functions.description: Adds a Next.js app to the distributed application builder.
functions.remarks:
This method configures the Next.js application for both local development and publishing.
In run mode, it starts the Next.js dev server with the correct port binding.
In publish mode, it generates a multi-stage Dockerfile using Next.js standalone output mode,
which copies `public/`, `.next/standalone/`, and `.next/static/` into a
Node.js runtime container.
The Next.js application must have `output: "standalone"` configured in `next.config.ts`
and a `public/` directory (even if empty) for the published container to build correctly.
The following example creates a Next.js app.
```
var builder = DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.AddNextJsApp("frontend", "./frontend");
builder.Build().Run();
```
functions.signature: addNextJsApp(name: string, appDirectory: string, runScriptName?: string): NextJsAppResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the Next.js app.

parameters.name: appDirectory
parameters.description: The path to the directory containing the Next.js app.

parameters.name: runScriptName
parameters.description: The name of the script that runs the Next.js dev server. Defaults to "dev".

functions.name: addNodeApp
functions.description: Adds a node application to the application model. Node should be available on the PATH.
functions.remarks:
This method executes a Node script directly using `node script.js`. If you want to use a package manager
you can add one and configure the install and run scripts using the provided extension methods.
If the application directory contains a `package.json` file, npm will be added as the default package manager.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the resource.

parameters.name: appDirectory
parameters.description: The path to the directory containing the node application.

parameters.name: scriptPath
parameters.description: The path to the script relative to the app directory to run.

functions.name: disableBuildValidation
functions.description: Disables deploy-time build validation checks for the Next.js application.
functions.remarks:
By default, `AddNextJsApp` adds publish prerequisite steps that verify
the Next.js configuration (e.g. that `output: "standalone"` is set). Use this method
to suppress those checks when the configuration is set dynamically or via an external
mechanism that cannot be detected by static file inspection.

functions.name: publishAsNodeServer
functions.description: Configures the JavaScript application to publish as a standalone Node.js server that runs a built artifact directly.
functions.remarks:
Use this method for frameworks that produce a Node.js server artifact during the build and recommend
running that artifact directly in production rather than invoking a package manager script at runtime.
The application source is still built using the configured package manager and build script; this method
only changes the publish-time runtime container shape.
The container files source path is automatically set to `outputPath` so that only
the built output directory is copied into the runtime container, not the full application source.

parameters.name: entryPoint
parameters.description: The relative path to the Node.js entry point to execute in the published container after the build completes, such as `.output/server/index.mjs` or `build/index.js`.

parameters.name: outputPath
parameters.description: The relative path containing the built runtime files to copy into the published container. Defaults to the application root.

functions.name: publishAsPackageScript
functions.description: Configures the JavaScript application to publish as a server that runs a package manager script at runtime.
functions.remarks:
Use this method for frameworks where the production server depends on packages resolved at runtime, either
from `node_modules` or from the Deno dependency cache. The resulting container includes the full
application with its production dependencies already installed.
This method is appropriate for frameworks like Nuxt (where `useAsyncData`/`useFetch` requires the
full Nitro environment), Remix (where `react-router-serve` is an npm dependency), and Astro SSR
(where the built entry point imports unbundled `@astrojs/*` packages).
For Deno applications the generated container runs `deno task <scriptName>` and copies the populated
`DENO_DIR` cache from the build stage, so whatever the build resolved is already present at runtime.
Unlike the Node.js and Bun package managers there is no separate production install step, because the build
stage runs `deno install` and `DENO_DIR` is carried forward as-is rather than being pruned.
`deno install` only resolves the dependencies declared in `deno.json` or `package.json`. An
import written as a bare specifier in source, such as `import { assert } from "jsr:@std/assert"`, is not
declared anywhere the installer can see, so it is fetched on first use and the container needs network access
at startup. The same applies to anything reachable only from inside the build script's own task command, which
Aspire cannot inspect. Add those imports to the `imports` map in `deno.json` if the container has to
start without network access.
For frameworks that produce a self-contained server artifact that does not require `node_modules`,
use `PublishAsNodeServer``1` instead for a smaller runtime image.

parameters.name: scriptName
parameters.description: The name of the script to run in the published container. For Node.js and Bun applications this is a `package.json` script; for Deno applications it is a task defined in `deno.json`. For example, `start` invokes the configured package manager's run command for the `start` script, such as `npm run start`, `pnpm run start`, `yarn run start`, `bun run start`, or `deno task start`.

parameters.name: runScriptArguments
parameters.description: Optional arguments appended after the script name at runtime, such as `-- --port "$PORT"`.

functions.description: Configures the JavaScript resource to use Bun as the package manager and optionally installs packages before the application starts.

parameters.name: install
parameters.description: When true (default), automatically installs packages before the application starts. When false, only sets the package manager annotation without creating an installer resource.

functions.name: withDeno
functions.description: Configures the JavaScript resource to use Deno as the package manager.

parameters.name: install
parameters.description: When `true`, creates an installer resource that runs `deno install` before the application starts. parameters.name: kind

functions.name: withDenoAllowAll
functions.description: Controls the blanket `-A`/`--allow-all` grant.

while generated containers default direct `run`/`serve` entrypoints to
`--allow-net --allow-env`. Calling this method with `true` explicitly emits `-A`
in both modes.

parameters.description: Whether to emit `-A`/`--allow-all`. Pass `false` to grant only permissions configured with `WithDenoAllow`.

parameters.name: kind

parameters.description: Optional values that scope the permission. When empty, all access of the selected kind is denied.

parameters.name: importMapFile
parameters.description: The import map file path.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: The inspector mode to enable.

parameters.name: hostPort
parameters.description: The optional inspector host:port value.

functions.name: withDenoLock
functions.description: Sets `--lock <file>`.

parameters.name: lockFile
parameters.description: The lockfile path.

functions.name: withDenoNodeModulesDir
functions.description: Sets `--node-modules-dir`, optionally with a mode emitted as `--node-modules-dir=<mode>`.

functions.name: withDenoNoLock
functions.description: Sets `--no-lock`, disabling lockfile use.

functions.name: withDenoRun
functions.description: Selects the `deno run <entrypoint>` mode (the default).

functions.description: Appends raw runtime arguments injected verbatim BEFORE the entrypoint. This is the escape hatch that gives full parity with `AddExecutable("name", "deno", workdir, args...)` for any flag not covered by a dedicated `WithDeno*` method.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: The runtime arguments to append before the entrypoint or task name.

functions.description: Appends arguments passed to the script AFTER the entrypoint. Deno forwards everything after the entrypoint to the running program.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: The script arguments to append after the entrypoint or task name.

functions.description: Selects the `deno serve <entrypoint>` mode for serving an HTTP entrypoint.

parameters.description: When true (default), automatically installs packages before the application starts. When false, only sets the package manager annotation without creating an installer resource.

parameters.name: installArgs
parameters.description: The command-line arguments passed to "pnpm install".

capabilities.name: withRunScript
capabilities.description: Adds a run script annotation to the specified JavaScript application resource builder, specifying the script to execute and its arguments during run mode.
capabilities.remarks:
Use this method to specify a custom script and its arguments that should be executed when the resource is executed
in RunMode.
capabilities.returns: The same resource builder instance with the run script annotation applied, enabling further configuration.

parameters.name: scriptName
parameters.description: The name of the script to be executed when the resource is run.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: An array of arguments to pass to the script.

capabilities.name: withYarn
capabilities.description: Configures the Node.js resource to use yarn as the package manager and optionally installs packages before the application starts.

parameters.name: install
parameters.description: When true (default), automatically installs packages before the application starts. When false, only sets the package manager annotation without creating an installer resource.

parameters.name: installArgs
parameters.description: The command-line arguments passed to "yarn install".

capabilities.name: disableBuildValidation
capabilities.description: Disables deploy-time build validation checks for the Next.js application.
capabilities.remarks:
By default, `AddNextJsApp` adds publish prerequisite steps that verify
the Next.js configuration (e.g. that `output: "standalone"` is set). Use this method
to suppress those checks when the configuration is set dynamically or via an external
mechanism that cannot be detected by static file inspection.

handleTypes.name: NodeAppResource
handleTypes.description: A resource that represents a node application.

handleTypes.name: ViteAppResource
handleTypes.description: Represents a Vite application resource that can be managed and executed within a Node.js environment.

capabilities.name: withViteConfig
capabilities.description: Configures the Vite app to use the specified Vite configuration file instead of the default resolution behavior.
capabilities.remarks: Use this method to specify a specific Vite configuration file if you need to override the default Vite configuration resolution behavior.

parameters.name: configPath
parameters.description: The path to the Vite configuration file. Relative to the Vite service project root.

memberDocs.name: Write

memberDocs.name: Import
